holidays.name: National If Pets Had Thumbs Day
holidays.description: Picture your cat opening the fridge, your dog working the TV remote, and your hamster typing out a strongly worded complaint about the wheel. Today you get to imagine all of it. Pets with opposable thumbs would be adorable, and also a little terrifying.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, lighthearted observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular pet-themed day on the internet.
holidays.funFact: Humans, apes and some monkeys have true opposable thumbs. Giant pandas get by with a wrist bone that works like a 'pseudo-thumb' for gripping bamboo.

holidays.name: Talk in Third Person Day
holidays.description: Today, you refer to yourself in the third person. Everyone will wonder why you are doing this, and you will happily explain that you are celebrating. Warning: this habit gets annoying quickly, and you will probably enjoy it anyway.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is listed on March 3 in holiday calendars and is meant to be silly.
holidays.funFact: Julius Caesar wrote his war memoirs in the third person. Athletes and politicians still do it today, and the habit even has a name: illeism.

holidays.name: National Cold Cuts Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble deli stack, from bologna and salami to turkey and ham. Pile them onto a sandwich, roll them up, or eat them straight from the fridge at midnight. No judgment today.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that falls each year on March 3. Its creator is unknown.
holidays.funFact: Bologna, a popular cold cut, is named after the Italian city of Bologna. Its ancestor is mortadella, a pork sausage that the city has made for centuries.
